entries.title: I Found the 20 Best Prime Day Tech and Gadget Deals (October 2026)
entries.summary: Never pay full price. Bag yourself some Prime Day tech deals on our favorite WIRED-tested gadgets.
entries.content:
Amazon’s Prime Day tech deals are here again. Yes, already. The economy is tough right now, and if you’re feeling this cost-of-living crisis, you probably don’t need that shiny new thing. But if you do need it, you certainly won’t want to pay full price. We put two pieces of research together for you: we track prices to make sure deals are actually deals and we only recommend stuff we believe is worth buying. Seriously: all the Prime Day tech deals you see here have been life-tested by the WIRED Reviews team in our own homes, often using our own families as guinea pigs.

If you haven’t found the deal you want yet, browse our roundup of the Absolute Best Prime Day Deals.

Updated on October 6 at 8:30 pm ET: Added some new tech deals and checked through the current products on sale.

  • Nothing’s Best Headphones: Nothing Headphone (1) for $189 ($110 Off)
  • Asus’ Marvelous Mesh Router: Asus ZenWiFi BT10 for $450 ($240 Off)
  • Samsung’s Most Powerful Smartphone: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra for $980 ($420 Off)
  • Apple’s Rarely Discounted MacBook: Apple MacBook Air for $1,099 ($200 Off)

Audio and TV Deals

The flagship Apple AirPods Pro 3 are its best wireless earbuds, and they're at the lowest price since June. Music sounds great, noise cancellation works well, and they offer excellent call quality. Apple added more ear tips for a better fit for small ears, new tools like heart rate sensing and live translation, and enhanced support for folks with hearing loss. If you use an iPhone, these are the wireless earbuds for you.

The Nothing Headphone (1) is one of our favorite pairs of over-ear headphones. With an attractive and distinctive design that combines a transparent look with tactile controls like a volume wheel and media control paddle, these headphones make a real statement. They also boast top-notch battery life. This is the best discount we’ve seen on them so far.

Prime Day is a great time to pick up older models at deep discounts. The Sonos Beam Gen 2 is a great example, having coming out originally in 2021. It's since been supplanted by the Sonos Beam Ultra, but that model is hundreds of dollars more (even while on sale!), and the Sonos Beam Gen 2 has never been cheaper. Our own audio expert, Harry Rabinowitz, used this model in his own home as his primary soundbar and found it to be a particularly good fit for smaller homes.

Phones, Wearables, and Accessories Deals

The Samsung S26 Ultra was the pick of the bunch this year, with a cool privacy screen, blazing performance, long battery life, and an excellent camera, but all three of Samsung’s S26 phones are on sale right now. These are the lowest prices they’ve been so far.

The Moto G Stylus is our pick of the best cheap phones under $400, and is is as low as it has ever been right now. If you miss a headphone jack and microSD card slot, this could be a winner. This is the 2025 model, but Motorola increased the price by $100 for the 2026 Moto G Stylus, and, apart from the upgraded active stylus, there’s little to justify the extra cost.

This is a solid smartwatch, and an especially great choice if you have a Samsung Galaxy phone. You can save yourself a significant sum by opting for last year’s model and Samsung’s Galaxy Watch9 is only a modest upgrade over the Watch8, considering it’s $120 more expensive.

Anyone with a trio of Apple gadgets (iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods) will benefit from snagging one of the best Apple 3-in-1 wireless chargers for their nightstand, and this is my top pick. The wide base keeps it steady, enabling you to remove your iPhone from the magnetic wireless charging pad one-handed, the Watch pad lets any strap dangle, and the base has a spot for AirPods, too.

This power bank does it all. I love the translucent design, offering a peek at the electronic innards. It has a handy display with comprehensive stats, and it supports just about every fast charging protocol going. It packs 24,000 mAh of power and can charge at up to 140 watts, so it will juice up anything from a laptop down. It’s even IP66 rated for water and dust resistance.

Want a hard-wearing, fast charging cable to keep your gadgetry juiced? This Anker cable from the best USB-C cables is our pick. It can deliver 240 watts, has a tough, braided nylon exterior made from 100 percent recycled plastic, and comes with a lifetime warranty. Anker promises this cable will last a century and it can operate in temperatures from -40 degrees to 176 degrees Fahrenheit. The ribbed cuffs make it easy to grip, and it’s USB-IF certified, too.

Computers and Home Office Deals

The M5 MacBook Air got a serious price hike at the end of June, bringing it up to $1,299. But this week, everyone’s favorite laptop dropped to $1,099, which is the lowest price it’s been at in months. It comes with 16 GB of RAM and 512 GB of storage, so you’re getting a really solid configuration that should last you many years. The 15-inch model is also $200 off if you need a larger screen to work on. Regardless, this is the best laptop can buy at the price price I’ve seen it at in a while.

Interesting in dipping your toe in the world of local, agentic AI? I know that will sound cringey to some—and trust me, I get it. But there's no denying the increasing interest in using the Mac Mini for just that, and the latest M6 is particularly good at it, as I learned in my own testing. Of course, the M6 Mac Mini has a broader appeal too, and it's great to see it on sale so soon after launching. If you need even more performance for your AI curiosity, you'll need the Mac Studio, which also received its first discount since launching, coming in at $150 under its retail price.

Gaming laptops have gotten far too expensive recently, so I was delighted to see that one of my favorite gaming laptops to recommend has a huge sale. The price on this has fluctuated wildly over the past few months, but never has it dropped to just $1,100. This is the model that comes with the entry-level RTX 5050, but it has a better display than every other gaming laptop in this price range. Also consider the RTX 5060 model for $1,499 at Walmart, which really takes performance to the next level.

If you don’t want another subscription in your life, the Asus ZenWiFi BT10 is the best mesh system for you. You get three bands of stable Wi-Fi 7 coverage for your home. A two-pack will cover most properties (up to 6,000 square feet), there are two high-speed 10 Gbps ports (alongside a Gigabit LAN and USB 3.0), and security software, parental controls, and extras like VPN support are included.

You won't find a better cheap monitor than this. That's always true of the Dell 27 Plus S2725HSM, but it's especially true at $130, which is the cheapest I've ever seen it at. It's just a basic 1920 x 1080 resolution, but the fully adjustable stand and great image quality gives this a major step up over every comparable monitor I've seen. If you've got some more cash to spend, I'd also recommend the upgraded 4K model, which is also on sale at a new low price.

A tidy, affordable pair of PC speakers, Edifier’s M60 is a bargain at its usual price, so this discount is not to be sniffed at. These speakers produce a surprisingly rich, clear sound that persists when you crank the volume, and there’s a thump of bass. They also come with angled stands, and connect via USB-C, 3.5 mm, or Bluetooth 5.3.

Tablets and E-Reader Deals

The best iPad for most people, if you don’t already have the iPad (11th-generation, A16), now is the time to buy. The 11-inch screen is perfect for kicking back on the couch with a book, game, or movie. It has a pair of 12-megapixel cameras, and Touch ID in the power button. It’s also handy for keeping the kids amused.

Fancy an e-reader that can also serve as a digital notebook? Amazon’s third-generation Kindle Scribe has you covered. It’s slim, with an 11-inch screen, smart stylus, and a bunch of AI features. It’s a go-to choice for note-takers and students. While we recommend the older model in our best Kindles guide, that’s mainly due to the lower price, and this is a better option when it’s on sale. Such as right now.

Home Tech Deals

If you’re looking for an easy security system and you don’t mind paying a pricey subscription ($10 per month or $96 a year for a single camera, $20 per month or $216 a year for unlimited cameras), Arlo is the way to go. This outdoor camera captures 2K video, has a 160-degree field of view, two-way audio, and direct Wi-Fi connection. It’s the best of the best outdoor security cameras. The Arlo app is fast, with rich notifications and two-factor authentication, so you can log in with your fingerprint or face, phone permitting.

Combining a white noise machine, sunrise alarm light, and clock into a single device designed to help lull you to sleep and wake you gently, Hatch’s third generation Restore is an all-in-one way to establish a healthy sleep routine. It also enables you to leave your phone outside the bedroom. It’s annoying that you need a subscription to unlock all the content, but if it helps you get a better night’s sleep, it’s worth it.

If you like to stay organized, this 27-inch smart calendar could be for you. You can sync calendars, organize your meal plans, create to-do lists, and see your family’s day-to-day laid out in a clear format. Smart calendars might not be worth it for everyone, and some features require a subscription (digital photo frame functionality, smart assistant, rewards), but this is a decent discount on the biggest model.

entries.title: 113 Best Prime Day Deals We’re Shopping This October (2026)
entries.summary: Amazon Prime Big Deal Days are here, and we’ve tracked down the best discounts on all the gear our team recommends.
entries.content:
Amazon’s fall Prime Day sale—also known as Big Deal Days 2026—is live. The sale starts today, October 6, and runs through midnight tomorrow. As with all Prime Day sales, you'll need to be an Amazon Prime member to take advantage of the discounts.

It may only be October, but it's never too early to jump on that holiday gift shopping. We've combed through all the deals and found the best ones, based on our years of testing and reviewing. WIRED's picks for the best Prime Day deals only include products someone from our team has personally tested and reviewed. We track prices using several tools to avoid falling for fake discounts. There are no shoddy knockoffs or overpriced products among our recommendations, just good deals on great gear.

WIRED Featured Deals

  • The best MacBook deal: MacBook Air M5 for $1,099 ($200 off)
  • The AirPods Pro 3 deal you’ve been waiting for: AirPods Pro 3 for $179 ($70 off)
  • The best deal for your morning routine: Philips Norelco OneBlade 360 for $35 ($15 off)
  • A colorful Kindle for less: Kindle Colorsoft for $190 ($100 off)
  • The best impulse buy: Anker Nano Power Bank for $20 ($7 off)
  • The best Bluetooth speaker: JBL Flip 7 Bluetooth Speaker for $110 ($40 off)
  • Our favorite digital wall calendar: Skylight Smart Calendar Max for $560 ($70 off)
  • An automatic espresso machine at an all-time low: De'Longhi Rivelia for $1,000 ($300 off)

Updated 8:30 pm ET October 6: We've added tons of fresh products on sale and checked through the already-listed deals.

Contributors: Louryn Strampe, Simon Hill, Nena Farrell, Kat Merck, Molly Higgins, Boutayna Chokrane, Luke Larsen, Harry Rabinowitz, Les Shu

Best Apple Deals

As someone who’s tested dozens of laptops this year already, I still find myself recommending the MacBook Air M5 more than any other. It’s the most well-rounded laptop you can buy, sporting great performance, long battery life, and a razor-thin chassis. The price has gone up considerably over the past year, but that’s true of many of the best laptops. And now, it's at its lowest price since June, making it an absolute must-buy and the top of my list for Prime Day laptop deals. —Luke Larsen

Apple AirPods Pro 3 are the best wireless earbuds for anyone with an iPhone. They’ve got best-in-class noise-canceling, an excellent transparency mode, clear and detailed audio quality, and a plethora of advanced features like built-in heart rate sensors and live translation. The heart rate sensors are particularly impressive—you can go on a run with just your phone and these earbuds and get accurate GPS, heart rate zone, and calorie data. —Harry Rabinowitz

The Mac Mini has been sold out for the majority of this year due to the rapid escalation of interest in using them as local, agentic AI machines. The brand-new M6 model is faster (and more expensive) than ever. But the fact that you can buy them at all right now feels significant, and Amazon has the best deal on the latest model you’ll find. —Luke Larsen

While almost all of Amazon's Kindles are on sale, the Colorsoft is one of the best. If you're looking to get the biggest discount on a new Kindle, the best sale is on the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft. It's the most expensive Kindle, but it also has the best discount during Amazon's sale event. —Nena Farrell

This is the lowest price ever for the Nothing Headphone (1), an excellent, stylish pair of over-ear headphones with great sound and even better battery life: up to 35 hours with noise-canceling on or 80 hours with it off. The headphones have tactile controls on each earcup I personally love—things like a volume wheel, Bluetooth pairing button, on-off switch, and media control paddle. —Harry Rabinowitz

The Google Pixel Buds Pro 2 remain our top earbuds for Android users (they also work with iOS). They're aesthetically pleasing. They sound great. They're comfortable and have a long-lasting battery and active noise cancellation, plus some useful software features. If you want good earbuds that aren't AirPods, these might be up your alley. —Louryn Strampe

Best Smart Home Deals

Amazon launched two new Echo Show smart displays last year, and the Echo Show 11 was easily the better of the two. The sound is better, and the screen is larger—but not so large that it's a pain to put on a kitchen counter. Amazon did raise the price by $30 at the end of August, but this is still the lowest deal price I've seen for it since its launch. —Nena Farrell

The Echo Studio has been our favorite Echo speaker for the sound quality since the original model, and the second-generation version packs fantastic sound like its predecessor. I also love that its price didn't increase between the two generations, or after Amazon's price hike in August. It's still one of the more expensive models, even on sale, so I'd choose it only if you have a massive room you're trying to fill with sound. But it's also the only new Echo that didn't get a price increase, so this sale isn't just a trick of the numbers. —Nena Farrell

A good smart plug is handy all over the house. I really like this set from TP-Link's Tapo brand because the plugs are Matter-certified, making them easy to pair with any existing smart home ecosystem, and have a small form factor so they won't block the other outlets. I like them best for controlling lamps that don't fit for a smart bulb, but you could use them for all kinds of things. —Nena Farrell

If you’re looking for a cheap automatic pet feeder in a home with two pets and you don’t need all of the bells and whistles, I recommend this model. It’s a solid, inexpensive dual feeder with a connected app where you can customize feeding plans of up to six meals a day, and it also has a knob on the front to plan meals if you want to go analog. Plus, I loved the hygienic stainless steel inserts that can be removed for easier cleaning. This is the lowest price we’ve seen all year.  —Molly Higgins

If you value aesthetics and still want a solid small-to-midsize room air purifier, you may like this discounted model from Windmill. It has a chic Scandinavian look, with bamboo paneling that makes it look more like furniture than most other models I’ve tested. It has an intuitive connected app that integrates with other products in the Windmill ecosystem. It also has an internal sensor and indicator light that make it easy to tell the air quality at a glance. —Molly Higgins

Laptop and Home Office Deals

When it comes to monitors, all most people need is something reliable, comfortable to use, and not horrifically ugly. That’s underselling the Dell S2725HSM, despite its price. It’s a basic 1080p resolution, but it has really solid image quality, and it even comes with a 144-Hz refresh rate. All those features are heightened when it’s on sale for just $130, too. That’s the biggest price drop I’ve seen on this monitor in a while. —Luke Larsen

Tilt-Pan-Zoom webcams like the Obsbot Tiny 3 are so much more than just a webcam for video calls. The gimbal gives the camera a huge range of motion, letting you dramatically expand what you can shoot compared to a standard webcam. It’s ideal for streamers, content creators, podcasters, and online educators—or really anyone who wants to show more of their room on video. On top of that, it also has tons of interesting AI features to play with. This is a rare discount on this top-shelf webcam, too. —Luke Larsen

This tri-band Wi-Fi 7 mesh is the best subscription-free mesh system for most people. A two-pack will be enough to cover most homes, and each router has two 10-Gbps Ethernet ports, one Gigabit port, and a USB 3.0 port. Asus allows you to tinker with and configure everything and offers comprehensive security software and parental controls at no extra cost (you can even redeem a free year of NordVPN service with this mesh).  Clip the on-page coupon to save. —Simon Hill

The Branch Ergonomic Chair Pro is both our favorite office chair and our favorite gaming chair. It's incredibly comfortable and features several points of adjustment so you can fine-tune your experience. It's also high-quality and easy to assemble. You can't beat the value offered for the price. —Louryn Strampe

This soundbar plus subwoofer is a fantastic way to upgrade your TV audio system for a reasonable price, especially at 25 percent off. The Polk Signa S4 is one of our favorite soundbars for that very reason: It’s simple, easy to use, sounds great, and doesn’t cost an arm and a leg. Sure, it doesn’t have more advanced features like Wi-Fi connectivity, voice assistant support, or multi-speaker surround sound. But if you’re coming from built-in TV speakers, this is a great first upgrade. —Harry Rabinowitz

This is our favorite portable Bluetooth speaker. It delivers huge sound, and is small and durable enough to carry on any adventure. It also has IP68 water resistance, an easy-release strap, and a two-hour battery boost (or four if you reduce the bass). —Louryn Strampe

I'm not going to act like 20 percent off is a huge bargain, but this is an iconic turntable and our number one pick from our best turntable guide. It’s durable, upgradable, and sounds great out of the box. Physically owning music, whether that’s vinyl or CD, is in vogue in 2026, and this USB-enabled turntable lets you plug in directly into your computer to rip your records to MP3 files. —Harry Rabinowitz

The best Samsung phones are on sale. If you want an Android phone with real power, but prefer something that’s not too big, the Samsung Galaxy S26 is tough to beat. It’s fast, has a bright and sharp screen, a reliable triple-camera system, and good battery life. You also get seven years of software support, and the base model has jumped to 256 GB of storage. This has been cheaper, but with prices on the rise across the market, I’m not sure when it will dip again. This is still a decent discount. —Simon Hill

My all-time favorite robot vacuum is often on sale, but this is the lowest the price it ever goes (and used to only go as low as $800, so don't miss it!) The Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal uses a UV light to spot stains and spills on your floor and will go back to scrub them away after doing its regular clean. It's the smartest one I've tried in 2026 by a long shot, and little announcements from the base station make it easy to know when the vacuum is just cleaning versus handling stains. —Nena Farrell

I usually see a lot of Dyson vacuums on sale during events like these, and the slightly older Dyson V15 is often one of them. Now that there are newer models, the V15's sale price is just under $600, and it's a good price for a Dyson vacuum that comes with both a hard floor and all-floor cleaner head, plus a crevice tool. There's an LCD screen too, which you won't find on Dyson's new, more affordable models. —Nena Farrell

This carpet cleaner looks like a normal vacuum, but it has two removable tanks: one for warm water and detergent, and another for the dirty water it extracts while wet-washing embedded grime. A pedal-activated spray jet helps target stains, and three modes—Max, Deep, and Express—let you adjust the cleaning. It also comes with plenty of attachments, including an upholstery attachment and a stair-cleaning tool. It’s a godsend for spill-prone kids and cats that love to throw up on soft surfaces, and it’s the lowest price we’ve seen this year. —Molly Higgins

If you’re looking to cut down on food waste but don’t want to deal with smelly compost containers and mess, FoodCycler 3 is one of my top picks for this purpose. Put your peels, cores, and wilted herbs into the included 3.5-liter countertop bucket; when it’s full, seat it right in the machine, which will then grind and dry your scraps to a fine powder. You can then top-dress your lawn with the resultant “Foodilizer,” put it in your yard waste bin, or even mix it with soil (1:10 ratio) to use in your garden. —Kat Merck

My parents bought this bread machine years ago because it was one of the only models with a ceramic pan and no suspicious nonstick coatings. They handed it down to me, and I still have it. It works flawlessly, turning out ball-shaped 1-, 1.5-, or 2-lb. loaves. It doesn’t have as much versatility as higher-end machines like the Zojirushi Virtuoso, which does a better job with specialty breads, but if you’re interested in making your own basic, preservative-free loaves without having to mess with starters, kneading, and all-day rising schedules, this machine is the best value out there. —Kat Merck

This is a solid deal on the best automatic latte and cappuccino maker we've tested. The Rivelia is user-friendly and easy to use, and it even has a built-in milk frother in addition to the grinder. We also like the touchscreen display and consistently tasty results. —Louryn Strampe

The wee little Lit Hero is GoPro's smallest, lightest, cheapest action camera. It's my favorite GoPro for selfies thanks to the included light. The cluster of four LEDs next to the lens ensures this camera keeps you well-lit in every scene. The Lit Hero isn't quite as capable video-wise as the Hero 13 Black (also on sale, see below), but it can shoot 4K at 60 fps, and the battery held up for a respectable 101 minutes during my test (shooting a 4K 60 fps video). —Scott Gilbertson

The Theragun Relief is our budget Theragun pick, and at $100, it’s an even cheaper buy. It’s an older 2023 model, but massage guns don’t need the latest features to be effective. You get three attachments and three speed settings, and it’s half the weight of the Pro Plus, making it much easier to pack for travel. entries.title: Jaguar Finally Reveals Its Biggest Gamble: the Type 01
entries.summary: Following a viral rebrand and two years without selling a new vehicle, the British marque takes the covers off the most divisive electric car yet seen.
entries.content:
The day has finally arrived. Jaguar began its long road to electric reinvention in November 2024 with a firestorm of a rebrand featuring no cars. Just a month later, it revealed a prototype: the Type 00—a car so polarizing it practically broke the internet’s automotive enclave. Some loved it; others hated it so much that Jaguar’s own staff were targeted for supposedly betraying the company’s 90-year history.

Since this chaotic but undoubtedly viral launch, major departures have followed, including Jaguar Land Rover’s (JLR) chief creative officer Gerry McGovern, the notable car designer who signed off on Jaguar’s divisive all-electric design and the no-car ad campaign.

Jaguar’s managing director, Rawdon Glover, is a brave man. Through this shitstorm, and a frighteningly long period of selling no new cars whatsoever, he’s remained unflappable; utterly confident that, when people see the final car—the finished version of the luxury four-door GT that is “like no other”—everything will make sense. That moment is here. The company finally revealed the Jaguar Type 01 at an event in New York City on Tuesday—the finished version of the Type 00. (Jaguar Land Rover paid a portion of WIRED's travel expenses so we could attend the launch.)

“A bold grand tourer that never arrives unnoticed, like all the best Jaguars of the past,” Jaguar’s press material says. This is most certainly true: you will see this thing coming. The low roofline, short front and extended rear overhangs, long hood, and huge 23-inch wheels all remain from the prototype, just as promised. The cab-rear design hides a 50–50 weight distribution, and the huge surfaces make it hard to square the fact that this is the most aerodynamic Jag ever, with active vanes, a deployable spoiler, and airflow trickery delivering a drag coefficient of 0.23 Cd.

Crucially, the production model’s extra doors make more sense of the design, shifting the Type 01’s look away from Thunderbirds territory to more familiar ground. The front has been softened ever so slightly as well, which again is preferable to the prototype’s exceedingly bluff nose. The rear, however, is where the exterior design really shines with hidden-until-lit, full-width lights embedded in horizontal strikethroughs.

Let’s get the specs out of the way: the Type 01 is the most powerful Jaguar road car, with up to 1,030 Pferdestärke (PS) and 1,365 Newton-meters. It goes from standstill to 62 mph in 3.2 seconds. Justifying the tagline of “power in reserve,” the car can rocket from 62 to 112 mph in a further 4 seconds. I’ve been driven in it, and it feels like the acceleration never ends thanks to the tri-motor setup of a 260-kilowatt (kW) front motor paired with twin 310-kW rear motors.

It stands 5,235 mm long and 1,403 mm tall, but all-wheel steering makes it feel much smaller on the road. The 850-volt bespoke Jaguar architecture and 118-kilowatt-hour usable battery supposedly deliver an EPA range of up to 400 miles (450 miles on WLTP), with a “sustained highway speed” range of up to 320 miles. Drivers can add up to 200 miles of range in 13 minutes using 350 kW rapid DC charging. So the TL;DR? It’s huge, fast, aerodynamic, powerful, and, most definitely, unique.

Inside, a dramatic central spine runs the full length of the cabin, creating a zone for each occupant. Lots of “brass-inspired” finishes are intended to underline the luxury message. A panoramic glass roof with adjustable virtual blinds brings in the light, but there’s no rear windscreen. Instead, a digital “ClearSight” rearview display is embedded centrally in the full-width panoramic soundbar at the base of the windscreen to show what’s behind. Cleverly, the feed from this rear-facing camera is positioned at the same height as the door mirrors, supposedly reducing the annoying focal adjustment these systems usually demand.

Ahead of the driver is a 24-inch OLED screen that extends toward the center of the car. A central 7-inch smartphone-style display sits between the driver and front passenger for common controls such as climate and audio, operated entirely by touchscreen with (sadly) no physical switchgear in sight. “Hot stone massage effect” seats, whatever those are, are also electrically adjustable in 12 different ways. Cabin air purification removes allergens, toxins, and particulates, and a fragrance diffuser offers a choice of scents—which seems to be the pinnacle of what Western auto companies think a luxury car interior needs these days.

As a grand tourer, luggage space is important. The Type 01 offers 450 liters of load space, expanding to 1,000 liters with rear seats folded. And then there are the production stories: Jaguar built more than 150 prototypes, drove 700,000 miles, and filed more than 360 patents while developing the car.

Jaguar is most proud, and rightly so, of its “impossible panel.” It's a single, unbroken panel that runs more than 3 meters from the A-pillar to the rear of the Type 01. Pressing this huge piece with five different acute angles in it was deemed not possible by Jaguar's modeling system. After roughly 22 weeks and 1,500 hours of development (supposedly requiring someone to come out of retirement), Jaguar realized this “impossible” panel.

Pricing of the Type 01 is possibly the most important thing Jaguar has to nail. Starting at around $170,000 (or £130,000—no confirmed pricing yet), this puts the Jag well below Ferrari Luces, electric Merc G-Wagens and Lamborghinis, and even the new Bentley Torcal, exactly where Glover wants to sit. Jaguar thinks it has a sweet spot in luxury EVs, a Goldilocks zone where buyers are eager to part with cash for electric cars that aren’t astronomical but priced high enough above the premium sector to be legitimately highfalutin.

No one has really succeeded with the luxury EV market. Porsche has tried. So has Lamborghini. Mercedes has had a very tough time. Now Bentley is having a crack at it. Glover thinks that the Type 01 has a shot.

“One of us is going to break through the glass ceiling and make a success of EVs at elevated price points,” Glover tells me. “The best way to do that is not to play into the tropes of EVs. You’re not going to get there because it’s an electric car. You’re going to get there because the car itself looks a certain way, feels a certain way, drives a certain way. If you can do all of those things, [it doesn’t matter] whether it’s combustion or electric. Just being an electric car was enough for such a short period. Cars have got to earn their right in somebody’s garage.”

Glover has openly said the Type 01 will have to earn its place with “almost an entirely new client base,” one that is supposedly younger, more affluent, urban, independently minded, creative, and wishing to “carve their own path.” We shall see very soon exactly what kind of person signs on the dotted line to reserve a Type 01. Will they look like the youthful, vibrant characters in Jaguar’s initial launch campaign, or like traditional Jaguar, Lotus, and Aston owners with gray hair, flannel shirts, and bad shorts?

“We’ve got to make sure that new audience comes along," Glover says. “But I don’t want to alienate anybody.” The Chinese do well with that youthful audience. “I’ve driven some of the Li Autos. I’ve driven some of the XPeng cars. They’re impressive in terms of the amount of technology in them. The quality of fit and finish is increasing at a pace.”

But Glover still thinks a big gap exists between Chinese cars and established Western autos; though with Xiaomi’s achievements after only a few years of making cars, it’s hard to see this view staying true for long. “They’re playing in a commodity space," he says. "It’s about how many features, how much tech, how much range, and how can I do it at the lowest price. I’m not saying we’re immune to all of that, but it certainly validates us getting out of the volume premium market.”

Like Bentley, Jaguar is leaning into its heritage to look for things the Chinese will find harder to emulate. But it could be argued that the Type 01 lacks any obvious heritage. The pioneering spirit is there, for sure, but this is an EV very much looking forward, not back. With that in mind, what does, say, two years of success look like to Glover for this electrified rebirth of the brand?

“Success will be we’ve established ourselves at the [new] price point,” he says. “People are saying, ‘Yep, Jaguar is worth paying more for.’ I know what volumes we need to achieve. I’m not going to articulate those, but just under that we need to generate a certain level of volume to create that critical mass.”

For Glover, this level of volume requires customers to see Jaguar as a more current, culturally relevant brand, and to be genuinely interested in what the company will do next.

“Is it just the man in the bad shirts and bad shorts, or have we actually been successful in attracting a new audience?” Glover says. “We start seeing that in the first two years.”

entries.title: You Probably Aren’t Going to Get the Plague
entries.summary: The death of a lab worker in Russia has authorities looking at whether plague played a role. Even if it did, though, the odds of it spreading are very low.
entries.content:
A mysterious death of a woman in Russia following a lab accident has stoked fears about plague spreading. But the odds of that actually happening remain very low, with the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention saying on X Tuesday afternoon that the circumstances of the case remain unconfirmed and that there is “no indication of a broader threat to the United States” at this time.

“We are working across the US government to assess developments as additional information becomes available,” the agency said. “CDC and our interagency partners are prepared and will continue to monitor the situation closely.”

Last week, a young researcher died from severe pneumonia of “unknown” origin after reportedly breaking a test tube at her workplace, the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute in Siberia. The hospital that treated her before her death was placed under quarantine, and her coworkers at the lab were isolated, according to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty.

Christian Lindmeier, a spokesperson for the World Health Organization, told reporters in Geneva on Tuesday that the group has been in touch with Russian authorities. Based on currently available information, WHO says the ​public health risk to the general population is very low.

“I think that’s the correct assessment,” says Gigi Gronvall, an immunologist and senior scholar at the Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security. “We don’t know anything about anything right now.”

Russian authorities have said contact tracing hasn’t yielded any signs of dangerous pathogens spreading, according to the Associated Press. Infamous for causing millions of deaths in Europe during the Middle Ages, plague is rare today. It is caused by the bacteria Yersinia pestis, which is found in wild rodents and their fleas in many parts of the world. It’s spread to humans through the bite of an infected flea and occasionally through direct contact with an infected animal. Antibiotics can cure plague, but they must be started as soon as an infection is suspected.

Pneumonic plague occurs when a person inhales infectious droplets that contain the bacteria. In July 2025, an Arizona man died from pneumonic plague after exposure to infected cats. It can also spread from person to person through respiratory droplets during close contact. But human-to-human transmission is rare, with the last reported occurrence happening in 1924 in Los Angeles. The possibility, though, is why the CDC says it’s important to rapidly identify cases and treat them.

“Once you know that somebody has been exposed to it, and even if you have a doubt that somebody has been exposed to it, you can immediately start antibiotics to prevent the person getting afflicted with the disease and to avoid the continuous spread of the disease,” says Rutul Dalal, an infectious disease physician at Penn State Health St. Joseph Medical Center.

Dalal says if the Russian lab worker did die from plague, he is confident that the disease could easily be contained. “With Covid, that was a virus we had not dealt with in the past,” he says. That required novel interventions, while “here, we do have antibiotics to deal with this.”

The incident also occurred in a remote part of Russia, which could naturally limit its spread. “Siberia is not exactly Paris,” Gronvall says. “There’s not a lot of travel going back and forth.”

Whether plague is the culprit or not remains an open question. Rospotrebnadzor, Russia’s federal public health and consumer protection agency, said “extensive” testing found “no microorganisms associated with the patient’s professional activities.” But the US has urged the country to share as much information as possible, while other nations that share borders or are near Russia, including Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan, have set up quarantine protocols.

entries.title: Best Prime Day Digital Wall Calendar Deals: Skylight, Everblog, Apolosign (2026)
entries.summary: Digital wall calendars can organize multiple family calendars, meal plans, chores, and to-do lists, and even double as a digital photo frame. And best of all, they’re on sale.
entries.content:
I test a slew of devices every year, but it’s rare that a category truly surprises me. I entered the world of digital wall calendars expecting to hate them, and I walked away their biggest fan. If you’ve been curious about getting one for yourself, now is the perfect time: Just about all of my picks are on sale.

If you’re unfamiliar, a digital wall calendar is a physical device that syncs all of your digital calendars onto its screen. No more grabbing your phone to check when the next appointment is or scribbling out plans that fell through. It’s great for couples and families who juggle multiple schedules and want to see them all in one place, on a screen the entire family can access.

But these devices don’t stop there. All my picks also act as an overall family hub, managing chores, meal plans, and more to make life a little easier. It’s the smartest device in my kitchen, though it isn’t a true smart-home device.

Here’s a collection of the best digital wall calendars I’ve tried and their sale prices for Amazon Prime Big Deal Days 2026. You can also check out my guide for more details, and don’t miss all our deal roundups this season.

The Best On-Sale Digital Calendars

The best deal is on Everblog’s HomeCal, which feels surprisingly similar to the popular Skylight Calendar without requiring a subscription to access every feature. The 21.5-inch device is often discounted from its $400 price tag to around $320, but you can get it for $280 at the time of writing.

I really like that this calendar has all the features I could want without any paywalls. You’ll get meal planning, chores, and to-dos on top of calendars, and you can also have it double as a digital photo frame for free. You can only upload one photo at a time, but a slower experience is well worth not paying a subscription fee.

If you’re looking to spend even less and still avoid a subscription fee, the Apolosign Digital Calendar is a great choice that’s also on sale for Prime Day. It’s available for the cheapest price out of my picks—just $249—with a 15.6-inch screen and options for either Apolosign’s Calendar Mode or Android Mode, which gives you more customization tools.

The Android Mode will allow you to add a photo screensaver so it can also function as a digital photo frame. This view makes it less calendar-focused, however; it feels more like an Android tablet. You’ll get to customize widgets, but it doesn’t sync as smoothly on this mode.

My all-around favorite digital wall calendar comes from Skylight, but my preferred option—the Skylight Calendar 2 with a 15.6-inch screen—has only certain colors on sale. It’s usually available on Skylight’s website for $300, though, so this discount isn’t outrageous. The Skylight Calendar Max, with its massive 27-inch screen, is on sale for a nice discount, but even this price is more than twice Apolosign’s, and some features are paywalled.

Still, it’s a great device, and Skylight’s original product is digital photo frames, so it’s no surprise that the photo feature works best on this one compared to other frames. The interface feels clean on both the device and companion app, syncs fairly seamlessly with my variety of calendars, and updates on its own with new features (and will give me a fun pop-up the next morning telling me what's new). I just wish it didn’t have a paywall and that the smaller, better-priced Calendar 2 had a bigger sale.

entries.title: The Best Anti–Prime Day Deals for Amazon Haters
entries.summary: Want to save money without supporting Amazon? This roundup is full of deals on WIRED-approved favorites.
entries.content:
Everyone is talking about Amazon’s October Prime Day. Good deals or not—maybe you don't want to shop at Amazon for whatever reason. Plenty of other stores, big and small, are hosting sales alongside Amazon this week. Everything below is hand-tested by WIRED and doesn’t have to be purchased on Amazon. You do you.

Apple AirPods 3

Apple AirPods 3 for $179 at Best Buy: If you want the best wireless earbuds for iPhone, you want the AirPods Pro 3. They have great noise cancellation and even built-in heart rate sensing and live translation.

Apple AirPods Max 2

AirPods Max 2 for $429: These are on sale for just $30 more than their lowest price ever, being price-matched at Walmart to match Amazon. The AirPods Max 2 are still pricey, with less battery life and software features than we'd like. But there's no denying that they're stylish, and the sound quality isn't bad either.

Kindle Scribe Colorsoft

Kindle Scribe Colorsoft for $520: This latest Kindle is being price-matched at Best Buy. It has an impressive 11-inch color display and can double as a digital notebook thanks to the included stylus. Unlike the Kindles you may have had in the past, this one is more of a do-it-all tablet than just a conventional e-reader. A new Kindle Colorsoft was just announced (and not yet available), but this deep discount makes it a great buy right now.

Sonos Beam Gen 2

Sonos Beam Gen 2 for $359: It's a few years old, but we've never seen the Sonos Beam Gen 2 drop to prices this low. These have been personally tested by our own audio expert, Harry Rabinowitz, who has complimented its excellent sound quality and compact footprint. And fortunately, Sonos has matched the Amazon discount, giving you another buying option. Walmart is selling it for the same price as well. —Luke Larsen

Furbo 360 Dog Camera

Furbo 360 Dog Camera for $54: Here's one of the few deals this week where the first-party retailer is cheaper than Amazon's Prime Day sale. This Furbo dog camera impressed our resident pet pro, Molly Higgins, who appreciated its full-color night-vision, two-way communication, and ability to pan in a full 360 degrees. It can even auto-track your pet around the room—and most importantly—dispense treats. —Luke Larsen

Native Union MagSafe Wallet

Native Union MagSafe Wallet for $39: The Shop app has a solid deal on WIRED Commerce Director Cooper Fleishman's favorite MagSafe wallet. It features space for up to three cards and has a sleek, unobtrusive footprint.

Stanley The Quencher H2.0 Flowstate Tumbler

Stanley The Quencer H2.0 for $45: I love this water bottle. It's sitting next to me right now! It keeps drinks icy cold all day, and it has stayed colorfast, you should hand-wash it if possible to preserve the finish. I like the large capacity too since I don't have to refill it as often. It's half-off on Shop, a great deal compared to what we usually see.

Quince Premium Down Comforter

Quince Premium Down Comforter for $164: This down comforter keeps me warm year-round and plenty toasty in winter. It's fluffy and warm, with a cozy shell that never lets any feathers poke through. It isn't very heavy, but it is very good at insulating you.

Shop Books, Locally

Amazon was first and foremost a book-selling store, so why not stick it to the man by buying your next book from Bookshop.com? It's an online book shop that lets you purchase online from local bookstores. And in celebration of anti-Prime Day, it's offering free shipping today and tomorrow. It's a great way to support independent bookstores and save on shipping fees to get physical copies of your favorites or your to-be-read pile.

I personally shop there when I want a physical book but don't want to leave my house to purchase it. It's also a good option for picking up gift books without needing to visit multiple stores.

entries.title: Best Prime Day Laptop Deals: Save Up to $500 (2026)
entries.summary: My favorite MacBook, gaming PC, and budget laptop are all on sale for Prime Day, some at the lowest prices I’ve seen in months.
entries.content:
Laptop prices have risen significantly over the past six months. The memory shortage wreaked havoc on prices, even causing Apple to hike them up in June. That makes deals on big shopping events like Amazon Prime Day even more important. For the retailer's Prime Big Deal Days fall sale, I've spotted a number of my favorite laptops among the dozens I've already tested this year.

So, whether you're looking for a new MacBook or a budget Windows device, you'll find some excellent picks below. In addition, check out more deals in our roundup of the Absolute Prime Day Deals and Best Apple Prime Day Deals.

MacBook Air (M5)

The MacBook Air is $200 off for Prime Day, bringing it to $1,099. That's the cheapest it's been since June. It's a remarkable deal compared to the competition, especially given the 512 GB of storage and 16 GB of RAM it comes with. Apple raised prices across the board on Macs this past June, but this discount reverses that issue entirely. This sale is on the latest M5 model, which came out this past spring and performed really well in all my testing. It's currently at the top of my recommendations not only as the best MacBook but also as the best overall laptop of any kind. That $200 discount applies to every configuration of the MacBook Air available on Amazon, including the larger 15-inch model.

Not only is this the MacBook I recommend to buy for most people, it's also the best laptop deal this week. Neither the MacBook Neo nor the MacBook Pro are being discounted by anything out of the ordinary.

Microsoft Surface Laptop 13.8

This is the best price on the latest version of the Surface Laptop since it launched. I've been tracking it closely, primarily because of how expensive it has been in comparison to the older model from 2024. The price difference always made me recommend the 2024 version, even though it had a slower Snapdragon chip inside. This discount, which is $500 off the retail price and $70 cheaper than it's ever been, brings it close enough to the price of the 2024 model to justify itself. The Snapdragon X2 Elite's GPU performance compared to the X1 model is significant enough to justify the extra money.

For what it's worth, though, the 2024 Surface Laptop 13.8-inch model is currently selling for $1,096, which is also a great deal. If you're trying to get your purchase closer to $1,000, I still think that model is one of the best Windows laptops you can buy.

HP OmniBook 5

The HP OmniBook 5 has been my favorite budget laptop for a while now. It avoids so many of the pitfalls of cheap Windows devices, including typical low-end screens, thick chassis, and poor battery life. This one has a beautiful OLED screen, is as thin as a MacBook Neo, and gets fantastic battery life, thanks to the Snapdragon X chip inside. The one compromise is the touchpad, which still isn't very good.

HP.com typically has the lowest price, which is $780 right now. But Amazon has that beat during Prime Day, at only $750 for the 16-inch model. Not only is it cheaper, but it also comes with 512 GB of storage, twice the amount as the discounted HP.com model. I should say that I prefer the 14-inch model, just because the 1920 x 1200 resolution looks a bit sharper on it.

Lenovo LOQ 15

This has long since been one of my go-to affordable gaming laptops to recommend for two very important reasons. First off, most budget gaming laptops have terrible screens. That's true of the Alienware 15, the MSI Cyborg A16, and even the Lenovo LOQ 15 Essential Edition—all gaming laptops in the same price range as the Lenovo LOQ 15. But the LOQ 15 display has good color coverage, so greens and reds don't look oversaturated. With that benefit, the LOQ 15 still tends to cost less than its alternatives, and for Prime Day, the RTX 5050 configuration is as cheap as I've seen it in many, many months. If you can increase your budget, the $1,499 RTX 5060 model at Walmart will deliver much better gaming performance, and I'd recommend it too.

Asus ZenBook A14

The Asus Zenbook A14 is known for being super light. It weighs only 2.16 pounds, about half a pound lighter than the MacBook Air. The difference is really noticeable, both in the hand and when toting it around in a bag. It also comes with an OLED display, a great touchpad, and a decent assortment of ports.

But like the Surface Laptop, the 2026 Zenbook A14 is too expensive. Unlike the Surface Laptop, it's not on sale for Prime Day. That's why I'd recommend picking up the previous model, which comes with a Snapdragon X Plus, 16 GB of RAM, and 512 GB of storage. The 2026 model offers more storage options, but it also has a much higher starting price. A slightly cheaper model is also available with the Snapdragon X, but the Snapdragon X Plus offers better multicore CPU and GPU performance.

entries.title: We’re Tracking October Prime Day Live (2026)
entries.summary: Our team is tracking Prime Day deals in real time. Here’s what’s worth buying today.
entries.content:
Our team is tracking Prime Day deals live to find all the best discounts and prices. Stay up to date with the latest coverage on all the sales we’re shopping ourselves.

It’s day one of Amazon Prime Day. The deals are fresh, the FOMO is young, and your shopping cart is still pretty empty. We’ve got two days to find the best deals, and we intend to bring you the sun, the moon, and the stars. Before you know it, these gizmos will be back at their outrageous full prices.

Our fabulous WIRED reviewers will be popping into this live blog throughout the day to yap about the stuff they’re buying and the bargains we think you should know about. We’ll also regularly be updating our Absolute Best Prime Day Deals.

That’s a Wrap on Day One's Deals

The first half of Prime Day is coming for an end, but we'll be back tomorrow with more great deals we've spotted and are even shopping ourselves. If you're hungry for more deals while you wait, check out our guide to the Absolute Best Prime Day Deals to see what's worth buying.

Everyone Needs to Hear About This Dish Soap I Bought

I, for one, always enjoy posts about what people actually bought for Prime Day, so I present to you the one thing I myself have bought: dish detergent. Apparently spray-on dish detergent has been around since 2020, but I just became aware of Dawn Powerwash this summer when I saw it on an endcap at the grocery store and bought it on a whim (typically I do grocery pickup to curb my impulse shopping, but this time it paid off!). I am not ashamed to admit that dish spray in a bottle has changed my life. It’s not only a no-mess, only-spray-what-you-need solution for dishes, but you can use it to clean all sorts of things, from clothes to your car. One bottle of Powerwash is $5 at most grocery stores, so not only are you saving $2 a bottle with this deal, it’s being delivered right to your house, so you won’t go to the store and impulse-buy other things. Win-win!

My Best Hair Ever Is Thanks To This Hat

It might look like a baseball cap, but this red light hat unlocked my best hair ever. I'm pregnant now and everyone has compliments for my hair, but I know the real source of this was my red light hat I religiously wore at the end of last year into this year. The HigherDose Red Light Hat transformed my hair from patchy into shiny and healthy, and my sensitive scalp stopped breaking out into itchy sections. Red light is currently not recommended for me as a pregnant woman, but I can't wait to rock this hat again next year to help me escape the postpartum uglies.

Chat, Should I Get My Husband a Smart Bird Feeder for Christmas?

I beg of you: nobody send this blog to my husband. He always manages to surprise me on Christmas morning with something thoughtful, and a smart bird feeder has been something I'm plotting to get him.

My husband and son love going on evening walks to see the animals and birds, but soon it'll get dark too early for him to enjoy them after a work day. The solution? A smart bird feeder that will record video they can enjoy together after dinner, seeing what birds came to visit. WIRED reviewer Kat Merck says this is the best-looking smart bird feeder she's tested, and it's got a nice discount for Prime Day.

Of All Things, a Multicooker Is Top of My Prime Day Wishlist

I have a problem. I'm obsessed with this slow cooker.

I already have a regular slow cooker and a multicooker at home, so I don't need this one. But I can't stop thinking about it. All I can think about is how fun it would be to have two things cooking side by side for holiday events, like two kinds of hot chocolate or mashed potatoes in one half with meatballs and gravy on the other. The pairings are endless, and I want it for every holiday party this season. Will I pull the trigger? I'll report back after Prime Day ends if I added it to my purchases.

Hatch Nightlights Have a Chokehold on My Nursery

I wrote this in our Smarter Buys newsletter last weekend, but my kiddo loves his Hatch Rest, which Hatch has now replaced with the Hatch Baby that's on sale for some small discounts (the deals are better off Amazon than on for this one). I find the noise and nightlight so comforting, I’m looking forward to testing the brand-new Hatch Sleep Clock, which seems to be for all ages. I also just found the Hatch Rest 2 in a non-Amazon refurbished deal, if you'd prefer the older model to the new.

Admit It. You Want the New Dyson.

Whenever I tell people I test vacuums (among other things) for a living, they immediately ask “Have you tried a Dyson? Is it really worth it?”

The short answer is yes. You really can feel a difference with Dyson’s powerful vacuums, but the price can still make it too much of a reach for plenty of people. The best Dyson experience is with the brand’s higher-end vacuums as well, and I was impressed that the Dyson V16 Piston Animal came with not only two different cleaner heads, but had an option to upgrade to Dyson’s newest Submarine mop head. It’s a powerhouse of a vacuum, and it’s on sale (both with and without the Submarine add on!) if it’s the one you’ve been dreaming of.

A Very Neutral Protein Powder

I’ve tried maybe six different protein powders, and this is the only one that doesn’t upset my stomach, so it’s been a repeat buy for over four years now. It’s a staple in any morning smoothie or emergency “oh no it’s 4 PM and I forgot to eat lunch” drink. It’s usually on sale, so this isn’t a huge discount, but hey, anything helps with kitchen staples. It comes in four flavors—I prefer the unflavored version, since I’m already adding plenty of sugar through fruits like bananas, mangos, and the like.

This Is the E-Reader Accessory I’d Buy a Fellow Reader

If you’re looking for easy birthday or Christmas gift ideas for a fellow reader who you know has some kind of e-reader device, I’ve got an easy gift for you. Strapsicle’s e-reader straps are on sale for Amazon Prime Day and can fit multiple e-reader devices. They're one of my favorite Kindle accessories, but I love that they're not limited to the Kindle ecosystem if you use a different e-reader. There’s one set for the six-inch base Kindles and Kobo Claras, and another for the seven-inch Kindle Paperwhite/Colorsoft and the Kobo Libra Colour. Both versions are on sale now, and come in a ton of fun colors that add a great pop to any e-reader (and are super comfortable!)

A Rug Good For Mother Earth (And Your Wallet)

I am literally obsessed with this rug. Every time people come over, they compliment it, and I have to blurt out, “It’s machine-washable, too!” I love this rug’s traditional pattern, inspired by Turkish folk art, that isn’t too busy. It’s woven from soft polyester chenille, which has an interesting, slightly fuzzy texture and resists stains and marks. I have it in the rust colorway, which adds a pop of color without being too flashy. It’s also OEKO-TEX and GRS (Global Recycled Standard) certified, so it’s kind to Mother Earth, too.

This Robot Vacuum Spotted So Many Stains on My Floor

If someone texted me right now asking which robot vacuum to buy during Prime Day, I know my answer. It’s the Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal.

I love this vacuum because it actually has the smarts it promises. I’ve tested more expensive vacuums that barely notice the dried spills on my floor or will just mark a single messy area, while the Shark’s UV light helps it find stains everywhere. It even found a spot on my floor I know I spilled orange juice on on months prior and I guess never properly cleaned. Thanks to the Shark, it’s clean now. It’s on sale for Prime Day and truly a great buy.

I’m Not Saying This E-Reader Will Save Your Marriage, But…

My dad group chat asked about the one thing they should buy for Prime Day 2026, and I had to go with the Kindle Paperwhite. If you like to read in bed, and maybe you have a spouse who’s trying to sleep, and maybe, hypothetically, your spouse gets mad when your light is still on, there’s really no better way to stay literate and partnered at the same time. And there’s no better time to buy a Kindle. Reading something actually good at night instead of doomscrolling: a fantastic little routine upgrade!

Digital Calendars Rule for Families. This One’s the Best Deal.

My favorite gadget this year has been a digital wall calendar, and that came as a big surprise to me. I tried one once before and hated it, and thought I’d feel that way about every version. Boy, was I wrong. These handy devices fit easily into my home to show me my family’s various calendars, our to-do lists, our meal plans, and even doubles as a digital photo frame (my favorite part!)

I’ve tried a lot of models since then, all of which I like better. Just about every single digital wall calendar I recommend is on sale, but the best deal for what you get is the Everblog HomeCal. It’s a smooth, simple interface that reminds me of Skylight, but you’ll get it for a little cheaper than Skylight right now and won’t have to worry about a paywall.

I Keep This Kinda Terrible Power Bank in My Car

This MagSafe power bank has a laughable 5,000-mAh capacity, which is paltry compared to the beefy batteries inside most of our phones. But while it won’t get you enough juice to scroll Instagram Reels while you avoid eye contact with cuties at the bar, it will get you enough to turn on your phone in a pinch if it dies while you’re out hiking in the wilderness. So I keep it around in case of emergencies, and the unobtrusive form factor doesn’t get in the way of bigger, more superior power banks inside my backpack or glovebox.

Prime Day Has Become My Maternity Stock-Up Session

I’m currently expecting my second child, and at almost six months pregnant, it’s time for me to face the music. That music is the fact that I can’t keep ignoring the large purchases I need to make…and that none of my pants fit anymore, just in time for it to get colder outside.

It makes Prime Day a pretty good opportunity for me and my growing shopping list. Right now, I’m checking out on the DaVinci Suzy Recliner Glider that the internet has promised me is a dupe for the popular Babyletto glider. I’ll be quick to judge if that’s accurate or not, but I’m thrilled to find it on sale and that it looks large enough for my preschooler to squeeze into it with me and baby if he wants to. I also stocked up on a few pairs of CRZ Yoga’s maternity leggings that have a $5 discount right now. It’s not a ton, but I’d rather save a little wherever I can, especially since I bought a couple of pairs.

It’s Never Too Late to Start Skincare

As I approach middle age, I realized it’s time to start taking better care of my skin. I finally boarded the K-Beauty train (thanks, Marshalls!) and found that eye patches do wonders for my face. The editors at our sister publication, Allure, recommend the Peptide Collagen Hydrogen Eye Patch from CosRx, a respected Korean skin care company. With vitamin B12 and hyaluronic acid to help soothe, smooth, and moisturize under the eyes, while peptides encourage collagen production and help tighten the skin. I’m looking forward to adding this to my nightly cleansing regimen, and with 33 percent off during Prime Day, it’s worth trying.

My Annual Wireless Earbuds Restock

Every year, I end up buying a new pair of wireless earbuds during Amazon Prime Day, and this year was no different. I somehow have three separate pairs of AirPods that only have the right earbud. And after hearing my colleagues rave about the low price of the latest Apple AirPods, I knew I’d have to keep the tradition alive. The noise-canceling and transparency abilities are touted as some of the best you can find in an earbud. I don’t really care about the extra features like a built-in heart rate sensor and live translation; I just wanted to have a left earbud again. And I’m betting that at the very least, these will.

There Is No Such Thing as Too Many Pillows

I needed more pillows this Prime Day; I'm hosting family this weekend and want them to be comfortable. But I am also a pillow maximalist and always want more pillow, so I don’t need a crazy excuse to buy more Coop Home Good pillows. I’ve been using them for over five years, and combined with my Leesa hybrid mattress, have been getting the best sleep of my life. Or I was before I became a dad, but no pillow can solve that sleep problem…

My Gift-Giving Season Has Already Started With a Cool Kid’s Birthday Gift

For me, the holiday gift-giving season kicks off the second October arrives. That’s because I spend half the month answering questions about what I’d like for my birthday (October Libras, rise up) and the other half shopping for my fellow fall birthday people. The first birthday to arrive is actually a friend of my son’s, and the first Prime Day purchase I got was for him.

We love all kinds of toy vehicles in this house, but my son’s current favorite is this flexible track set and speedy little cars with LED lights built into them, making them easy to spot if my son sends them flying off the track. The flexible track is easy to make into a ton of shapes or add obstacles to, making it a fun choice for curious kids. It also feels like a fun, unique car instead of the usual packs of hot wheels or massive remote control vehicles to gift to a friend. It has a nice little discount right now for Prime Day, and a perfect thing to grab if you're shopping for kids ahead of a birthday or the holiday season.

The unique folding design features a universal magnetic enclosure and a pull tab for easier card access. The backing also pops out to form a kickstand for hands-free video watching on your phone.

We think this is the best USB hub for connecting your gadgets. Its 140 watts of power can handle larger devices, including gaming laptops that need more juice. It also offers nearly every port you might need, all clearly labeled on its sturdy metal chassis.

Best Deals on Home Tech

This video doorbell is heavily discounted right now. At first, I thought the $29 price was a typo. We love the Arlo 2nd Gen: It delivers crisp, consistent HDR video and a wide field of view with 180-degree coverage. Animated video previews help you quickly identify important alerts as they arrive. It also connects to your smart home ecosystem, such as Alexa and Google Home, and you can pair it with smart displays or speakers to announce callers.

I don't want to believe it, but winter is coming. As temperatures drop, one of the best ways to keep colds at bay and your home comfortable is to invest in a humidifier. You don't even have to spring for an expensive one—I bought a $40 humidifier for my bedroom last winter, and it was one of the best decisions I made. I got sick less, had fewer sore throats, and my skin didn't feel as dry (especially my lips).

This compact monitor and thermometer measures and displays PM2.5, AQI, temperature, and humidity. It measures only PM2.5 particles and uses US EPA Standards to calculate the AQI. It has eco mode for longer battery life, A mode, which samples air every three minutes, and real-time mode, which samples air every 1.5 seconds for the most accurate air quality readings. It's not the sharpest on the market, but it can measure both indoor and outdoor environments and operate within a range of -14 to 140 degrees Fahrenheit.

In Azul, you must make mosaics by matching tiles with different patterns and colors to get the maximum possible score. Azul is easy to grasp but supports many different tactical approaches and has surprising depth, making it one of the best family board games. At $16 off, this is the lowest price we'll see until Black Friday sales.

This addictive strategy game has become an icon in its own right. It challenges you to gather and trade resources to build and settle a board of hexagonal tiles, requiring both strategy and a bit of luck with dice rolls. It works best with three or four players, and unlike Monopoly or Dungeons & Dragons, you can finish the game in an hour. If you've been looking to spice up family board game night or to find a new game to share with friends, it's 45 percent off right now.

We like this building kit for older kids who want a more complex, hands-on experience. With this 175-piece set, you can build a four-cylinder engine that comes to life (when batteries are inserted) with moving pistons, valves, gears, and light-up LEDs to help kids understand how engines work.

I have persuaded everyone in my life to upgrade and can report no regrets from anyone who has followed my advice. One of my friends calls her robot vacuum her marriage-saver, while another friend loves hers so much she bought one for each floor of her home. Upgrading your stick vacuum can also make a huge difference—I had a friend test the new Dyson V8 Cyclone against her old V8, and she could immediately tell a difference.
